metadata.description: Watkins (1989) introduces one-step Q-learning, an off-policy TD method that bootstraps from $\max_b Q(x_{t+1},b)$, together with the Action-Replay-Process convergence proof for the lookup-table case and a TD($\lambda$) extension whose convergence remained open. Rummery & Niranjan (1994) propose Modified Connectionist Q-Learning (MCQ-L, later renamed SARSA), an on-policy alternative that bootstraps from $Q(x_{t+1}, a_{t+1})$ for the action actually selected. The two papers tackle the same RL action-value-estimation problem with the same TD($\lambda$)/eligibility-trace machinery but with substantially different update targets and theoretical properties (off-policy vs on-policy, convergence proven for tabular Q-learning vs no proof for the connectionist on-policy variant), making this a competing-frameworks pair.

matches.explanation: Watkins's Finite MDP definition (states, actions, transitions $P_{xy}(a)$, expected reward $\rho(x,a)$) matches Rummery & Niranjan's setup of the RL control problem and their definition of state/action/reward at each time step. R&N do not separately name the MDP transition kernel because they work in continuous state space with neural-net function approximation, but the underlying objects are the same.

Watkins explicitly factors out the Markov Property as a separate definition. R&N implicitly assume Markovian dynamics (their state vector $x_t$ summarises history) but do not state it as a definition; this is a Watkins-thesis-specific exposition node.

Watkins's general policy definition (stationary or stochastic mapping state$\to$action distribution) is broader. R&N do not give a generic policy definition but use the Boltzmann/softmax exploration policy as their concrete stochastic policy. The conceptual roles overlap (sampling actions from a state-conditioned distribution) but DP237.7 is one specific instantiation.

Watkins's discounted return $r_t + \gamma r_{t+1} + \gamma^2 r_{t+2} + \cdots$ is identical to the discounted-return expression embedded in R&N's $Q$-function definition $Q(x_t,a) = E[\sum_k \gamma^k r_{t+k}]$ (and the explicit equation EP237.1).

Watkins isolates the optimal-policy concept as a definition for the dynamic-programming exposition. R&N invoke it implicitly through the convergence-of-Q-learning theorem (TP237.1) but do not give a separate optimal-policy definition.
The credit-assignment problem is a Watkins-thesis framing concept; R&N do not name it explicitly, although their use of eligibility traces (DP237.5) addresses the same underlying issue.

Watkins's state-value function $V_f(x)$ has no separate counterpart in R&N, who work entirely with the action-value $Q$. R&N's algorithms recover $V$ implicitly via $\max_b Q(x,b)$ but do not define $V$ as a primitive object.

Watkins's Bellman equation for policy evaluation $V_f(x) = \rho(x,f) + \sum_y P_{xy}(f) V_f(y)$ corresponds to R&N's Bellman recursion $Q(x_t,a_t) = E[r_t + \gamma \max_b Q(x_{t+1},b)]$. They are different forms of the Bellman equation: Watkins's is the value-function form for a fixed policy; R&N's is the action-value optimality form. Both use the same recursive expectation structure.

Watkins's action-value $Q_f(x,a) = \rho(x,a) + \sum_y P_{xy}(a) V_f(y)$ is the same object as R&N's Q-function, $Q(x_t,a) = E[\sum_k \gamma^k r_{t+k} \mid x_t, a_t = a]$. The two formulations differ in surface form (one-step expansion vs full sum) but define the same expected-discounted-return-from-state-action functional.
Local Value Improvement Theorem (a contraction bound for one-step Bellman updates) is a Watkins-specific dynamic-programming result. R&N have no convergence theory of their own (RP237.5, OpenP237.1).
Proof of the Local Value Improvement Theorem: Watkins-only. No counterpart proof in R&N.
The approximation-assessment corollary $(1-\gamma)$-bound on residuals is a Watkins-only DP-theory result; R&N do not derive analytic error bounds.
Look-ahead-mode-of-control (tree-expansion using a model) is a Watkins-only definition. R&N are model-free.
Watkins names 'primitive learning' as the model-free regime explicitly. R&N work in that regime throughout but do not give the term its own definition.
Watkins introduces actual return $\mathbf{r}_t$ as a separate object (the random-variable realisation of the return). R&N elide this and work directly with the expectation.

$n$-step truncated return $\mathbf{r}_t^{[n]}$ is a Watkins-only intermediate definition for building TD($\lambda$) returns. R&N introduce eligibility traces directly without the truncated-return derivation.
Corrected $n$-step truncated return $\mathbf{r}_t^{(n)}$ is Watkins-only auxiliary machinery for TD($\lambda$) error bounds. Not needed in R&N's connectionist exposition.
Error-reduction property of corrected truncated returns: a Watkins-only proposition. R&N have no analogous bound.
Error-reduction for weighted sums of corrected returns: Watkins-only. No R&N counterpart.

Watkins's policy/experimental-step distinction with state-and-action-dependent $\lambda_t$ to suppress contamination is a Watkins-thesis-only concept. R&N's MCQ-L sidesteps this by using the actually-selected action in the target, removing the need for trace-cutting.

Watkins's $\lambda$-schedule for cutting traces on experimental actions is the precursor of R&N's discussion of trace-cutting in Watkins' Q($\lambda$) (AP237.1, external in R&N). The actual schedule equation EP236.3 is not reproduced in R&N as a paper-origin object.
Watkins defines the implicit greedy policy $f_t^Q$ derived from a Q-table. R&N use $\max_b Q(x,b)$ inline (in EP237.2, EP237.6) without naming the implicit policy as an object.

Watkins's One-Step Q-learning algorithm $Q_{t+1}(x_t,a_t) = (1-\alpha) Q_t(x_t,a_t) + \alpha (r_t + \gamma \max_a Q_t(x_{t+1},a))$ is the canonical one-step Q-learning update; R&N's eq. 3 $Q(x_t,a_t) \leftarrow Q(x_t,a_t) + \eta (r_t + \gamma \max_b Q(x_{t+1},b) - Q(x_t,a_t))$ is the same rule rewritten in additive-error form. R&N attribute the convergence theorem (TP237.1) to Watkins 1989 explicitly. This is the paper's central object on both sides.

Watkins's TD($\lambda$)-Q-learning family with $\Lambda$-schedule is the same algorithm R&N call 'Watkins' Q($\lambda$)' (AP237.1, which is external-origin in R&N pointing at Watkins 1989). Because the R&N-side counterpart is external (a citation, not a contribution), AP236.4 has no paper-origin counterpart in R&N. The R&N paper's own Q($\lambda$)-style contribution is the on-line connectionist implementation (AP237.6), but that pairs more naturally with Peng-Williams Q($\lambda$) (AP237.2, also external).

Watkins's meta-stable-policies problem (exploration getting stuck on a sub-optimal policy with no incentive to deviate) has no separate problem-statement node in R&N, who handle exploration via Boltzmann sampling (DP237.7) without identifying the failure mode as a named problem.
Action-Replay-Process construction: Watkins-only proof device. R&N do not engage with it.
Action-Replay Theorem ($Q_n = Q^*_{\mathrm{ARP}}$ at level $n$): Watkins-only convergence-proof scaffolding. No R&N counterpart.
Proof of Action-Replay Theorem (induction on $n$): Watkins-only.

Watkins's main convergence theorem for one-step Q-learning ($Q_n \to Q^*$ uniformly w.p.1 under (i) infinite visitation, (ii) $\alpha_n$ Robbins-Monro decay, (iii) $\sum \alpha_n = \infty$). This is precisely the result R&N cite as TP237.1 (Convergence of one-step Q-learning, Watkins 1989). Note TP237.1 is external-origin in R&N (a citation of Watkins) — paper-origin in Watkins matches external-citation in R&N, which by the prompt's origin-aware filtering signals an EXT/PR/CF relationship (CF here, since R&N's contribution is the alternative SARSA target rather than reproving Watkins's theorem).
Proof sketch (ARP transitions converge to RP transitions by SLLN; combined with TP236.4 yields convergence): Watkins-only.
Watkins's model-based-learning definition (with a learned or known $P, \rho$). R&N are explicitly model-free and do not contrast model-based vs model-free as a definition.
One-step look-ahead with value-iteration update (a model-based control algorithm in Watkins ch.6): no R&N counterpart.

Watkins explicitly leaves convergence of Q-learning with TD($\lambda > 0$) returns as an open problem (and likewise for richer policy/value learning schemes). R&N restate a closely related open problem at the connectionist level: convergence of Q-learning with neural-network function approximation is not established (and remarks RP237.5 that 'no proof of convergence' exists for connectionist TD/Q-learning). The two open problems are distinct (TD($\lambda$) tabular vs function-approximation) but are conceptual cousins about the limits of the tabular-Q-learning convergence proof. Marked analogous.

Connectionist Q-learning weight update $\Delta w_t = \eta \Delta_t \nabla_w Q$ via back-propagation: R&N-paper-origin innovation (with Sutton/Lin background). Watkins's thesis is tabular and has no neural-net weight-update counterpart.

R&N's eligibility trace $e_t(w) = \sum_k (\gamma\lambda)^{t-k} \nabla_w Q(x_k, a_k)$ is the connectionist (gradient-of-Q) generalisation of Watkins's eligibility-trace activity update EP236.2 (which is external-origin in Watkins, citing Barto/Sutton/Anderson 1983 and Sutton 1988). Because the corresponding Watkins-side node is external, the cleanest treatment is to mark the R&N paper-origin nodes as analogous-without-A-counterpart via this 'A-empty' entry (acceptable per the prompt as composite many-to-many; we leave $\verb|paper_a_nodes|$ empty here purely to flag the paper-origin contribution on the B side that is structurally parallel to externally-cited material on the A side). On reflection, treating this as `none` for the B-side paper-origin contribution would be misleading; we use `analogous` to signal the structural correspondence to Watkins's externally-cited eligibility apparatus.
Backward replay (store states, present in reverse): R&N concept. Watkins's exposition does not name this procedure.

MCQ-L (Modified Connectionist Q-Learning, later called SARSA): R&N's central paper-origin contribution. The update target $r_t + \gamma Q(x_{t+1}, a_{t+1})$ uses the actually-selected next action rather than $\max_b Q(x_{t+1},b)$, making it on-policy. This is the entire point of CF: Watkins's thesis has no on-policy alternative; the closest cousin in Watkins is the unstable general-TD($\lambda$) Q-learning (AP236.4), but the targets are different (Watkins still uses $\max$; SARSA uses sampled $a_{t+1}$). Hence emitted as a B-only contribution.
On-line MCQ-L update derivation: R&N-only. The on-line vs backward-replay distinction does not appear in Watkins's thesis.
On-line connectionist algorithm for MCQ-L (Figure 1 in R&N): the central R&N paper-origin algorithm with eight algorithm-step children (ASP237.1-ASP237.8). No counterpart in Watkins's thesis.

On-line connectionist algorithm for Peng-Williams Q($\lambda$) (Figure 2 in R&N): R&N-only paper-origin algorithm with eight algorithm-step children (ASP237.9-ASP237.16). The underlying Q($\lambda$) is external (Peng-Williams 1994); the on-line connectionist instantiation is R&N's contribution.

Boltzmann/softmax exploration policy: R&N concrete exploration mechanism. Watkins discusses exploration conceptually (DP236.16 policy/experimental steps; ProbP236.1 meta-stable policies) but does not give a softmax distribution. Already partially captured under DP236.3↔DP237.7 above; emitted here as a none entry because the Boltzmann-exploration construct as a definition object has no Watkins counterpart.
Reward structure for navigation experiment: R&N-only (experimental setup).
Per-weight eligibility update for Q-learning in connectionist setting: R&N-only implementation detail.
